summary: Remote WebSocket relay pipes messages into a local PTY on the installer host
details: The package establishes a persistent WebSocket connection to a hardcoded remote relay (default wss://msclaude.ai) and dispatches inbound `terminal_input` messages into a locally spawned node-pty session running `process.env.SHELL || /bin/bash` (or `powershell.exe` on Windows). connection.js routes those messages into terminalManager.write(...), and terminal.js spawns the shell via pty.spawn in the installer's working directory, giving any party that obtains the session URL (and optional password) arbitrary command execution on the installer's host. tunnel.js additionally accepts `tunnel_request` and `tunnel_ws_open` frames from the same relay and proxies HTTP/WebSocket traffic to 127.0.0.1:<port> on the installer's machine for any port present in a user-managed allowlist at ~/.agentlink/tools/proxy-config.json, allowing the remote party to reach local services once a port is enabled. The remote-control channel is the package's advertised purpose, but the mechanism is a network-to-PTY dataflow that constitutes a full-host backdoor by construction.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
